name: Telegraph cryptic crossword, All New book 4 No 34

book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Entire group ready

blocks.note: entire means all of it
a set is a group of things that belong together

explanation.surface: A whole team or party declares itself prepared to go.
explanation.definitionFit: All set is an everyday phrase for prepared and able to start at once.

clue.text: Radioactive element dispersed warm nuclei

indicators.note: things dispersed are scattered about, so these letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A radioactive substance scatters its hot atomic cores.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrencium is a synthetic radioactive metal, element 103, named after Ernest Lawrence.

clue.text: Inthis in the original position it's possibly posh

definitions.note: the clue's own 'In' completes the phrase 'in situ'

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the letters may be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
U means upper-class, the posh end of 'U and non-U'

explanation.surface: Some item kept where it first stood might be thought rather grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inthis' is 'In this' run together in the scan: put the answer after 'In' and you get the Latin phrase meaning in the original place.
explanation.definitionFit: In situ is Latin for 'in its place', used of something left where it was found.

clue.text: Treatment sore head needs?

blocks.note: surface reading: a remedy for a headache
setter's reading: a sore head is tender to the touch, and also deserves gentle, kind treatment

explanation.walkthrough: The word means both soreness to the touch and loving care, and a sore head both has the one and needs the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderness is gentle, caring treatment, and also the soreness felt when a bruise is pressed.

clue.text: Mistaken belief of fellow with everything, account to pay finally

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word it follows, keeping only that letter

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
all means everything
AC is the abbreviation for account
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A man who thinks he has it all is wrong, as the bill finally comes due.
explanation.definitionFit: A fallacy is a false idea or misconception, often one based on faulty reasoning.

clue.text: Nota lot of notice

blocks.note: first meaning: a small amount
second meaning: to catch sight of

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nota' is 'Not a' run together in the scan. The surface reads as one phrase about attention, but it splits into a small amount and a verb for seeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a little bit of something, and to spot something is to notice it.

clue.text: Battle in the last war

blocks.note: surface reading: the most recent war, such as the Second World War
setter's reading: the final conflict at the end of the world, as foretold in Revelation

explanation.walkthrough: 'The last war' sounds like the most recent one, but it means the war to end all things.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Revelation the place of the final battle between good and evil gives its name to that conflict.

clue.text: Inside beehives trying to find room

indicators.note: inside says the letters lie within the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: Beekeepers searching for space within the hives.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestry is a room in a church where vestments are kept and clergy robe.

clue.text: Make very angry when divorcee became separate

indicators.note: the word that follows turns into something else, so its letters take a new form

blocks.note: a former spouse is an ex
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is infuriated when a former partner decides to split off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Separate' looks like the end of the story about the divorce, but it is the letters to be rearranged after EX.
explanation.definitionFit: To exasperate is to irritate someone intensely, a verb matching 'make very angry'.

clue.text: Pulverised parking lot on which building stands

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the noun: the land a building occupies

blocks.note: something pulverised has been ground to powder
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A car park has been flattened to rubble before construction begins.
explanation.definitionFit: A ground plot is the patch of land on which a building is erected, its site or footprint.

clue.text: Lady having a socially acceptable set of books

blocks.note: taken as written
U means upper-class or socially acceptable, as in 'U and non-U'
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A genteel woman owns a respectable library.
explanation.definitionFit: An aunt is a female relative, so 'lady' serves as a loose example of the word.

clue.text: America's responsibility?

blocks.note: surface reading: a duty that falls to the United States
setter's reading: the possessive becomes a preposition plus the country's initials, so the burden rests upon America

explanation.walkthrough: Split as ON US, the answer literally says the burden rests on the US; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or duty, the formal word for a responsibility someone must bear.

clue.text: Keeps supply in drawer completely unmoved

blocks.note: a shop that stocks goods keeps a supply of them
a till is a cash drawer

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper keeps a reserve of cash in the register.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means perfectly motionless, so it fits 'completely unmoved' in the physical sense.

clue.text: Sway with constant music

blocks.note: to rock is to sway to and fro
steady means constant, unvarying

explanation.surface: Swaying along to a steady beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocksteady is a genre of Jamaican popular music, a forerunner of reggae, so it is an example of music.

clue.text: 15_ — _Is this how flaming row was started?

definitions.text: Is this how flaming row was started?

blocks.note: surface reading: a furious argument

blocks.clueFragment: Is this how flaming row was started?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a fire begins with a spark, so a heated quarrel would be started the same way

explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints stray characters '15_ — _' before the clue; the clue proper begins at 'Is'. 'Flaming' is both angry and literally on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: To spark something off is to set it going, the idiom drawn from lighting a fire with a spark.

clue.text: Do this to ensure one's still in harbour

definitions.text: Do this to ensure one's still in harbour

blocks.note: surface reading: making sure you are still there later

blocks.clueFragment: Do this to ensure one's still in harbour
blocks.note: setter's reading: a ship lowers its heavy weight to the seabed to stay motionless at its mooring

explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' means motionless, not 'yet': the ship stays put rather than drifting.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop anchor is to let the anchor down so a vessel holds its position.

clue.text: Busybodies leaving vehicle behind mistakenly disregard others

indicators.note: with 'behind', it says a word departs and stays out of the letters
completes 'leaving ... behind', so the named thing is abandoned and removed
done in error, so the remaining letters come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written
a bus is a vehicle, removed from the front

explanation.surface: Nosy people abandon their car and wrongly ignore everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking BUS out of BUSYBODIES leaves YBODIES, whose letters rearrange to DISOBEY.
explanation.definitionFit: To disobey is to ignore the orders or rules of others, a verb fitting 'disregard others'.

clue.text: Musicians' container?

blocks.note: surface reading: an instrument case or crate for a group of players
setter's reading: a group of musicians is a band, and a container is a box

explanation.walkthrough: A bandbox is really a light round box for hats or collars; the question mark admits the musical reading is a pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandbox is a cylindrical cardboard storage box, so it is a container, with 'band' read as musicians.

clue.text: Logo has misrepresented type of fuel

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown in a false form, so the letters are wrongly arranged

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A company's emblem gives a false picture of the fuel it sells.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasohol is a motor fuel blending petrol with ethanol, a kind of fuel.

clue.text: Kate's smock entangled round chimney

indicators.note: something twisted and wound about itself is in disorder, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: A woman's loose overall gets caught on a chimney pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A smokestack is a tall chimney, especially one on a factory or steamship.

clue.text: Neatly-trimmed tree

blocks.note: first meaning: smart and tidy in appearance
second meaning: an evergreen conifer

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one picture of a clipped hedge or topiary, but the two words define the answer separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce means smartly neat, and a spruce is a conifer used for Christmas trees and timber.

clue.text: Arkwright did not take in a single boarder

definitions.text: Arkwright did not take in a single boarder

blocks.note: surface reading: Richard Arkwright, the 18th-century inventor of a spinning machine

blocks.clueFragment: did not take in a single boarder
blocks.note: setter's reading: the builder of the ark took animals aboard two by two, never singly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Arkwright' reads as the inventor's surname but means the maker of the Ark, and 'boarder' is a passenger boarding, not a lodger.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the patriarch built the Ark and brought animals aboard in pairs, so no passenger came alone.

clue.text: 'It floats right back

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
aft is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Something buoyant bobs straight back up to the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' suggests reading something in reverse, but here it simply means the stern of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat buoyant structure of logs or planks, a thing that floats.

clue.text: Inwhich steps are taken by fencers?

definitions.text: Inwhich steps are taken by fencers?

blocks.note: surface reading: people putting up fences, or horses jumping them

blocks.clueFragment: Inwhich steps are taken by fencers?
blocks.note: setter's reading: fencers wield blades, and the steps are dance steps danced over crossed blades

explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'Inwhich' is 'In which' run together in the scan. A sword dance is a Highland dance stepped over crossed swords.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword dance is a traditional dance performed among or over swords, and fencers are people who fight with swords.

clue.text: What one on stage perhaps did in Los Angeles

definitions.text: What one on stage perhaps did

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the place name that follows

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A performer appeared in a Hollywood show, as performers perhaps do.
explanation.walkthrough: The city looks like part of the definition's story, but it is the fodder: loS ANGeles.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing is something a stage performer may do, and the past tense matches 'did'.

clue.text: Onestill on border at one end

blocks.note: read as 'One still': one is A, and still means but, as in 'but even so'

explanation.surface: Someone is stationary on the frontier at its far end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Onestill' is 'One still' run together in the scan; 'still' looks like motionless but means nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to adjoin or touch along a boundary, especially end to end.

clue.text: Becoming less angry during period allowing for change of mind

definitions.text: period allowing for change of mind
definitions.note: the word is used attributively, as in a cooling-off period

blocks.note: first meaning: calming down after a temper

blocks.clueFragment: period allowing for change of mind
blocks.note: second meaning: the legal window in which a buyer may cancel a contract

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the consumer-law term, a span after signing when a purchase can be cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooling off is calming down, and a cooling-off period is the statutory interval in which a deal may be reversed.

clue.text: Will be tense

blocks.note: surface reading: someone is going to feel nervous
setter's reading: the words 'will be' are a grammatical tense, the one for time to come

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like nervousness but is the grammar term; 'will be' is an example of that verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb form built with 'will' is the future tense in English grammar.
